reason: Five independently regenerated original-based variants executed and engine checked; major visual improvement in continuous source-derived foam/crest silhouettes, but no candidate validated for production owing to excessive stitches/trims and pictorial thread direction issues.
hypothesis_tested: ARTISTIC/TOPOLOGICAL: derive contiguous source-faithful crest/foam and organic cloud masses via LAB quantization of original, spatially cleaned connected regions, while protecting lighthouse/lantern/boat/sails/rigging as distinct semantic identities; compare selective directional guides and cleanup/hidden-travel variants.

workflow.provenance_note: Verified binary built on successful main parent commit; current main adds MCP distribution and its own CI was still running; no claim this binary matches current main.

method: Every variant rebuilt technical source from SHA-verified private original with deterministic source LAB k-means, median/bilateral cleanup, protected manually reconstructed lantern/boat geometry, independent semantic family map; native CLI digitize to fresh OSP, canvas set, inspect-derived semantic rename, render/check/diagnose/fidelity/density/export/stats. V3 additionally applied directional_guides to 3 inspected wave objects.

visual_review.v1: Best provisional source-detail legibility: coherent breaking wave and foam masses; 872 trims and many fragmented tatami regions.
visual_review.v2: Fewer cuts, lower hotspot area; slightly weaker fine details.
visual_review.v3: Three directional regions show stronger curved thread flow but also artificial concentric swirls and more cuts/hotspots; rejected.
visual_review.v4: Hidden-travel plus moderate island cleanup only modestly reduces trims; still cluttered.
visual_review.v5: 197 objects and 677 trims, strongest technical economy but smooths away fine Turner texture; not visually proven superior.

artifact.contains: Five actual OSP/DST/segmentation/semantic maps/engine previews/inspect/check/diagnose/fidelity/density/stats, reproducible source processing scripts, comparison report and metrics

changes: Five real source-regenerated OpenStitch experiments with same-project OSP/DST and real preview.
Private archive verified in Library; attempted separate private comparison image upload but upload was rejected (403 trusted producer), comparison remains only in current sandbox.
No main modification, no merge, no PR.
lessons: Quantizing the verified original into source-derived connected color masses restores coherent foam and wave silhouettes, unlike prior isolated gestures.
Native project digitize embeds the technical image so project fidelity is measurable, but that metric does NOT establish fidelity to original artwork.
Semantic object IDs assigned by inspect+rename are approximate ROI labels; native color segmentation still not a full semantic importer.
Three directional_guides wave objects add thread flow but also +54 trims versus V1 and slightly more hotspot area.
Even the simplest V5 has 137197 stitches and 677 trims; large background tatami and disconnected islands dominate physical risk.
Check returned zero errors with 51 warnings for every variant; physical stitch-out not attempted.
next_hypothesis: TECHNICAL/ARTISTIC: make dark fabric intentional negative space by subtracting unneeded sky and sea background fills before stitch generation, preserving source-derived connected foam carrier silhouettes and protected lighthouse/boat; apply selective manually guided directional details only where visually justified. Aim major reduction in 137k-145k stitches and 677-926 trims without losing the Turner composition; audit overlap/underlay and test small satin candidates only on locally suitable shapes.
